item.title: Delta Killings: Police summon Omo-Agege, Egbo, others for questioning
item.description: *Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters, eyewitness insists By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor The police yesterday summoned former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Area Chairman, Jaro Egbo and others for questioning over the political violence that erupted during a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA of Delta State on Monday. The violence has triggered fresh accusations of political intimidation, police bias and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. While the NDC yesterday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu, accusing the police of failing to protect its members, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, called on President Bola Tinubu to renounce what it described as dangerous political rhetoric. On a day that supporters of the camps staged protest and counter protest over the killings in Ughelli, Delta State governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, who visited the troubled community, condemned the killings and directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible. The state government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area. The attack occurred on Monday during a political campaign event involving former deputy president of the Senate and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Four persons were confirmed dead, while the NDC said no fewer than 15 others were receiving treatment in intensive care. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered an immediate, impartial and evidence-based investigation, including an examination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue. However, Vanguard gathered that one of the four supporters of Omo-Agege, killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had his first child barely six months ago. Yesterday, conflicting casualty figures trailed the killings. with rival political camps claiming seven deaths, against six acknowledged by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the police. Ughelli North Chairman, Chief Jaro Egbo, who hails from Uduere, named three persons he said were killed on his side, including the community’s President-General, PG, Cosmos Ejovwoke. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, on the other hand, listed four members of his campaign organisation died. The competing accounts bring the number of claimed fatalities to seven, although the governor and police put the toll at six, pending investigations. This was as former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, retd., warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections, which claimed over 800 lives, urging political parties, security agencies and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to protect the 2027 electoral process. item.title: South-East 400-km $100m gas pipeline, recipe for region’s industrial growth — SEDC
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu For decades, businesses and industries across Nigeria’s South-East region have depended on generators for their daily operations at a high cost. From the manufacturing clusters in Aba, Abia State, to the industrial workshops in Nnewi, Anambra State, the commercial centres of Onitsha, the business communities of Enugu and the productive enterprises of Imo and Ebonyi states, they all face the high cost and unreliability of electricity, forcing them to spend millions of naira to power their generators just to ensure that they remain in business. It has not been easy for a region whose economic strength is deeply rooted in entrepreneurship, manufacturing, commerce, and small-scale industries. Indeed, the energy challenge remains a major obstacle to industrial expansion as they spend huge resources powering their factories. All of them, including small businesses, struggle with rising operational costs. Will the proposed 400-kilometer South-East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project, with an initial investment budget of approximately $100 million, be a game changer for them? This initiative by the South-East Development Commission, SEDC, is planned to connect natural gas resources around the region to industrial and commercial centres across the five states in the region. It was unveiled at the South- East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony in Enugu on October 27, 2026. The initiative is a partnership between SEDC and GasSync Limited, NNPC Gas Marketing Limited and other stakeholders. President Bola Tinubu, represented at the ceremony by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt., Hon. Benjamin Kalu, described the project as an important step towards addressing the infrastructure deficit which has constrained the productive capacity of the South-East region. “There is a sound familiar to every manufacturer in Aba, Nnewi, Onitsha, Enugu and across the South-East. It is the sound of a generator,” Tinubu noted, adding that the resilience of South-East entrepreneurs should no longer be an excuse for inadequate infrastructure. “Our manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than on expanding production. Our young entrepreneurs should not find that the greatest obstacle to their ambition is the cost of keeping their machines running,” he pointed out. According to the President, Nigeria’s natural gas resources should be measured not merely by what lies beneath the soil but by the factories they power, the jobs they create and the prosperity they bring. A 400-km economic corridor At the heart of the initiative is a proposed regional gas distribution network designed to connect the Assa North-Ohaji gas processing project in Imo State to major industrial and commercial centres across the South-East. item.title: Greenwich Bank opens Warri, Uyo branches, targets five more cities
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Greenwich Bank Limited has opened branches in Warri, Delta State, and Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as it targets five additional cities in its nationwide expansion drive. The new outlets bring its physical network to seven, following the opening of five branches in Lagos, Ondo and Ekiti states in October. The Bank plans to extend its operations to Asaba, Port Harcourt, Abuja, Benin and Ibadan in the coming months. Speaking at the commissioning of the Warri branch, Group Chairman of Greenwich Holdings, Kayode Falowo, described the Niger Delta as a strategic market, citing its economic importance and entrepreneurial potential, particularly in oil and gas, maritime services and logistics. He said: “Warri’s economic prospects extend beyond its natural resources to the entrepreneurs, traders, contractors, service providers and other businesses driving commercial activities in the region.” At the Uyo branch commissioning, Chairman of Greenwich Bank, Segun Oloketuyi, said the commercial banking licence would enable the institution to extend its 32 years of financial services experience to farmers, traders, civil servants, students and entrepreneurs. He identified credit facilities, agricultural and SME financing, trade and treasury services, salary solutions and digital banking as key offerings. Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Fidelis Telije, urged residents, particularly small businesses, young entrepreneurs and women-owned enterprises, to take advantage of the Bank’s services. Similarly, Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Emem Almond Bob, said the Uyo branch would improve access to banking services and credit, support business growth and potentially boost the state’s internally generated revenue. Managing Director of Greenwich Bank, Benson Ogundeji, said the branches would deepen customer engagement and bring financial solutions closer to businesses and individuals. He identified oil and gas, maritime services, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, logistics and SMEs as priority sectors, adding that the Bank would combine physical branches with technology-driven solutions to promote enterprise growth and financial inclusion. Greenwich Holdings has over three decades of financial services experience, with interests in commercial banking, capital markets, asset management and securities. item.title: Political Violence: Dying for nothing as a Nigerian politician?
item.description: By Jide Ajani From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Over a dozen were said to have been injured. Mind you, in an outburst of emotive frustration about happenings inthe political sphere, the self-same Omo-Agege had used the phrase ‘ ig and die’. He was to later clarify that he was merely drawing attention to the need for credible elections. A bloody inheritance Political violence has accompanied Nigeria’s political evolution almost from independence. The January 15, 1966 military coup was a defining bloodbath. item.title: FirstBank redefines personal lending experience with mApply, mServe
item.description: FirstBank has launched mApply and mServe, two digital solutions that are transforming how customers access and manage Personal Loan Against Salary (PLAS) facilities. The launch marks a significant milestone in FirstBank’s personal lending journey as, for the first time in the Bank’s history, eligible customers can initiate a personal loan application digitally without having to visit a branch to begin the process. Previously, accessing a PLAS facility required customers to engage the Bank through the branch or their Relationship Manager. With mApply, FirstBank has digitised the application journey, giving eligible customers the convenience of applying through the Bank’s digital channels from wherever they are. Through mApply, customers can initiate their PLAS application, provide the required document, select their employer and preferred branch for processing, and submit their request digitally. The solution significantly reduces the reliance on physical documentation and branch visits at the application stage, creating a simpler and more convenient route to accessing personal credit. PLAS is available to eligible salary account holders domiciled with FirstBank, as well as employees of eligible organisations seeking to move their salary accounts to the Bank. Customers can access up to N150 million, with repayment tenors of up to 72 months, subject to applicable terms and conditions. FirstBank is also extending the digital experience beyond loan application through mServe, its self-service solution for customers with existing PLAS facilities. With mServe, customers can view their loan details and outstanding balances, monitor their facilities and update relevant information, providing greater visibility and control over their loans without having to rely solely on branch-based servicing. Together, mApply and mServe create a more connected digital experience across the PLAS journey. While mApply simplifies how customers initiate and submit new loan requests, mServe provides existing borrowers with a convenient way to manage and monitor their facilities. Both solutions are accessible through FirstMobile and Lit App, bringing personal lending into the same digital environment customers already use for their everyday banking needs. item.title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock investment opportunities in Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing the need for a tax system that supports innovation, enterprise growth and wealth creation. The Service noted that the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required regulations that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate. Speaking at the just concluded high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos, Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, described the creative economy as one of Nigeria’s most promising economic assets, noting that it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunities. Adedeji who was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha, also said that digital platforms had transformed how creative value was produced and commercialised, with entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands and digital products. He reiterated that tax administration must evolve to accommodate these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. “The government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said. Adedeji added that the new tax laws offered an opportunity to establish a more efficient system through clearer regulations, reduced compliance burdens for small businesses and improved taxpayer support. He identified clarity, understanding and value as essential to effective taxation, stressing that formalisation should provide creative businesses with tangible benefits, including access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection. The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event. item.title: Edo Police parades security operative for allegedly leaking information to cultists
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — THE Edo State Police Command said four members of the Edo State Security Corps, ESSC, have been arrested for allegedly leaking information to suspected cultists to enable them evade arrests. The Command’s spokesperson, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this while parading 16 suspects arrested across the state in connection with various criminal activities. The suspects, Isaac Irú we, Ashem Gideon, Tony Okhiale and Venture Uzu were arrested at Evbhomore community, in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state. They were accused of leaking information on police movements to cultists, enabling them to escape arrest. According to the Command, operatives of the Anti-Cultism Unit acted on intelligence on cult initiation activities in Benin City and immediately swung into action. “Upon getting there, we discovered that someone was giving out information on our movement to these cultists who escaped arrest. “Further investigation revealed that these men are members of the Edo State Security Corps, and four of them have been arrested and they are in our custody.” The command said investigation was still ongoing to ascertain their roles in the secret cult organisation. item.title: Petrol imports crash 52% as crude, wheat top Lagos ports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Imports of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol, through Lagos ports plunged by 52.23 per cent in November, while crude oil and bulk wheat ranked among the leading commodities imported through the ports in October and November. According to the Shipping Position document obtained from the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), PMS imports fell to 73,895 metric tonnes in November from 328,231 metric tonnes recorded in October. Crude oil imports through Lagos ports also dropped sharply, with 702,254 metric tonnes recorded in October, while no crude oil import was recorded in November. Bulk wheat ranked among the major commodities imported through Lagos ports during the period, with a combined 461,190 metric tonnes recorded in September, October and November. The breakdown showed that wheat imports rose to 252,348 metric tonnes in October and declined by 17.24 per cent to 208,842 metric tonnes in November. Other commodities on the import chart included 402,126 metric tonnes of PMS, 209,000 metric tonnes of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, 212,700 metric tonnes of bulk sugar, 150,000 metric tonnes of aviation fuel and 114,263 metric tonnes of bulk salt. Bulk sugar imports stood at 109,350 metric tonnes in October and 103,400 metric tonnes in November, while bulk salt imports rose from 33,000 metric tonnes to 81,263 metric tonnes over the same period. The document also showed that 624 trucks, 157 transformers and three Rubber-Tyred Gantry (RTG) cranes were received through Lagos ports during the period under review. item.title: FCMB Group’s pretax profit rises 103% to N272.8bn in 9mths
item.description: FCMB Group Plc reported pretax profit of N272.8 billion for the nine months ended September 30, up 103% from N134.5 billion a year earlier, driven by improved interest margins and a lower cost-to-income ratio. Annualised return on average equity rose to 30.1% from 22.4% a year earlier, while annualised return on average assets rose to 3.9% from 2.3%. Gross earnings for the same nine-month period rose 21% from a year earlier to N1 trillion, while after-tax profit increased 85.7% to N232.9 billion from N125.5 billion. Annualised earnings per share rose to N4.59, up 15% from N3.99 for full-year 2025, despite the expanded share base post-recapitalisation. The group’s unaudited results include the audited results of its Nigerian banking subsidiary – First City Monument Bank Limited. Commenting, FCMB Group’s Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Ladi Balogun, said he expects fourth-quarter earnings to benefit from a seasonal increase in digital lending and payments and lower operating expenses after the group recognised the full 2026 Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria levy in the first nine months. “With nine-month RoE at 30%, we expect full-year RoE to be materially above an earlier guidance of 25%, providing a strong foundation for further profitable growth and sustained shareholder value creation,” Balogun said. FCMB Group’s interest income rose 23.4%, while interest expense fell 3% as low-cost deposits made up a larger share of customer deposits. Net interest income rose 52.3% to N534.2 billion from N350.8 billion a year earlier, and net interest margin rose to 12.3% from 10.1%. Operating expenses rose 12.5% to N268.9 billion from N239 billion a year earlier, while the cost-to-income ratio fell to 43.5% from 55.5%. item.title: Osun man tortures 21-yr-old son to death over N75,000, phone
item.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo —The Osun State Police Command has said it arrested a 48-year-old man, Ogunniran Kayode over alleged murder of his son, Raphael, at Faaji, Odo-Otin Local Government Area of the state. A statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, yesterday, stated that the police received intelligence on October 19, 2026, that the suspect tortured his 21-year-old son to death. Then he buried his body in a shallow grave. Following the intel, the statement disclosed that the operatives of the command swung into action and arrested the suspect as he confessed to the killing of his son. “During the interrogation, he stated that his son stole a sum of N75,000 and absconded with one android phone he bought for him on easy buy to an unknown place. “And being a member of Iru-Ekun Security Network, he was able to get the son arrested through the help of his colleague.” “The case was then transferred to Homicide Section for further investigation”, the statement added. Meanwhile, operatives of the homicide unit visisted the crime scene and the shallow grave, where details and pictorial evidence of the torture were retrieved. The state Police Commissioner, Ibrahim Zungura, therefore, warned individuals with criminal intent to desist from the act or face full wrath of the law. item.title: No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports alleging that $2.04 billion realised from crude oil cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for, insisting that all transactions were fully reconciled. The company said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were set off against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to Nigeria under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme. In a statement by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, NNPC said the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes did not indicate missing funds. “No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” it stated. Under the DSDP programme, participating traders lifted crude oil in exchange for refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market. NNPC explained that while crude was priced in dollars, products supplied were sold in naira, with transactions reconciled and captured in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. The company said all 59 cargoes referenced in the reports were accounted for, adding that 30 were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then designated Federal Inland Revenue Service dollar account. On Duke Oil’s ownership, NNPC said it was incorporated in 1989 as its wholly owned trading subsidiary, adding that the relationship was documented in its corporate history, audited financial statements and NEITI’s 2023 industry report. It maintained that transactions between the company and its subsidiaries were disclosed as related-party transactions under International Financial Reporting Standards. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, but warned that it reserved the right to take legal action against publications it considered false or misleading. item.title: CBN holds MPR at 23%, says external reserves drop temporary
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, dismissing concerns over a decline of over $300 million in external reserves as a temporary, seasonal movement. Governor of the CBN, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, disclosed this yesterday at a press conference announcing the outcome of the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in Abuja. The bank also retained the standing facilities corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR, Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and Non-TSA public sector deposits at 75 per cent. Explaining the decision to retain the policy rate, Cardoso said: “In reaching its decision, the committee acknowledged the continued decline in headline inflation, but remained mindful of lingering upside risks, particularly those arising from the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could sustain pressure on energy prices. “In addition, the MPC observed that the anticipated increase in spending from the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could impact aggregate demand with likely upward pressure on prices. “Nevertheless, the committee judged that maintaining the current policy stance is appropriate to safeguard the gains of disinflation so far achieved, while remaining data-dependent and vigilant in taking further appropriate measures.” He added that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply associated with the harvest season would further strengthen the disinflation process. Cardoso said headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, reflecting sustained exchange rate stability and improved monetary policy transmission. “However, given the prevailing headwinds, which have slowed the pace of moderation in price pressures, members were of the view that maintaining the current policy stance would further anchor inflation expectations and support the disinflation process,” he said. On concerns over the decline in external reserves by over $300 million, Cardoso said the movement was not a source of worry, describing it as seasonal. “Our reserves is in a very strong position. So, that, I want to say, has not changed. And in actual fact, I believe it will continue to improve. What you mention is something that is transient,” he said. He explained that portfolio investors tend to recalibrate their positions towards year-end, while domestic users also increase demand for foreign exchange to hedge against future uncertainties. “These are all seasonal issues. And of course, with the elections coming, there’s more spending that is going on. These are all seasonal. And we believe very strongly that as we go into the next year, we will find a major moderation in the volatility that you have seen,” he said. item.title: Tears as victims of Bayelsa boat mishap get mass burial
item.description: By Emem Idio YENAGOA — It was tears and wailing at the Azikoro Cemetery in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, yesterday, as victims of Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state, were laid to rest in a mass burial. The burial, which commenced at about 11am, ended at 4pm, when the last batch of bodies, wrapped in black plastic bags, were brought to the cemetery in ambulances. The exercise was supervised by the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Nimibofa Ayawei, and the Commissioner for Environment, Mr. Ebi Ololo, alongside other government officials. The cemetery was enveloped by a foul stench from the bodies, some of which had begun to decompose, as grieving relatives, friends and sympathisers gathered to witness the burial. Many mourners broke down in tears, while others stood in groups, speaking in hushed tones as the remains of their loved ones were lowered into shallow graves. One of the bereaved relatives, Timipreye Diepreye, who said she lost seven family members in the tragedy, faulted the manner in which relatives were informed about the mass burial. She said the family would have made arrangements for coffins for their deceased relatives, particularly those whose bodies were recovered on Friday, if they had been adequately informed ahead of the exercise. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Community Development Committee, CDC, of Ukubie community, Mr. Ruben Kemelate, said the tragedy had plunged the entire community into mourning, with hardly any family left untouched by the loss. Kemelate, who disclosed that his elder sister also died at the Federal Medical Centre, said the scale of the tragedy had left the community devastated. He said: “We are in a very sad mood. Every family is affected. There is no family that is not affected. Like me particularly, my elder sister died in the FMC. So, every family is in a sad mood. We are in a very sad mood as a community. “So far so good, we have recovered 35 bodies and we have buried 29. We buried one on the first day, one seven-year-old boy. item.title: Campaign Violence: INEC awaits police case files to prosecute offenders
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has asked the Nigeria Police Force to speed up the arrest, investigation and transmission of case files against perpetrators of campaign violence, so the Commission can prosecute them directly. The INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, said swift action was necessary so that “impunity is decisively checked before January.” He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the Inspector General of Police’s Interactive Session with Chairmen and Secretaries of Political Parties on a peaceful electoral process before, during and after the 2027 General Elections. The session held at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peace Conference Hall, Force Headquarters. According to a statement by the commission, last night, Amupitan said INEC was “deeply concerned by isolated incidents of campaign violence, intimidation, and attacks on political rivals, journalists, and electoral facilities.” No election, office, or partisan interest is worth the loss of a single Nigerian life. Achieving a peaceful political environment is a collective national responsibility, not the duty of a single institution”, he added. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had “significantly strengthened legal deterrence,” adding that Sections 96 and 97 prohibit inciting campaign rhetoric and ban the use of thugs, private armed guards or masquerades at political rallies. According to him, the Act prescribes penalties of up to ₦5 million or twelve months’ imprisonment for individuals, and up to ₦10 million for political parties, on initial breaches. “Under Section 148, INEC is empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receipt of completed case files,” he said, explaining the Commission’s request for prompt transmission of the files by the Police. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, and other federal security agencies. Amupitan reminded political parties that INEC guidelines required them to notify the commissioner of police in writing of rally venues and times, and to submit the details to the Commission at least ten days in advance. item.title: South-East governors working for my re-election — Tinubu
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu, on Monday, told the Igbo community and their leaders, in Lagos, that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term. He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027. He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians. President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders, and Ndigbo leaders during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State. He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria. To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time. “I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country. “It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president. I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. “Though tribes and tongues may differ, we stand in brotherhood. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born. “Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians. “Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering. A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said: “President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.” He mentioned Chief Chidi Anyaegbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi; Doris Uzoka-Anite; and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people with whom he has close connections. On his part, the host Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, appealed to Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the President of massive votes from the state in the January 16, 2027, presidential election. Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the President, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend. item.title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
item.description: Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home. Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels. Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points. Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart. Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net. Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club. Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions. “That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal. Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively. Como and Betis flying Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia. Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game. Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross late on. It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli. item.title: Bakassi Port, border reforms to unlock Cross River’s economic potential – Customs boss
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, has said the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port and planned modernisation of strategic border corridors will unlock Cross River State’s economic potential, boost regional commerce and reposition the state as a major gateway for international trade. Adeniyi, who spoke at the 6th AfSNET Investment Conference 2026 in Calabar, Cross River State, said the state was on the path to reclaiming its historic position as one of Nigeria’s foremost commercial hubs. He described the groundbreaking ceremony for the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port as a significant milestone that could transform the economic fortunes of Cross River State and strengthen its participation in international trade. Reflecting on Calabar’s commercial heritage, the Customs boss recalled that the city once hosted Nigeria’s busiest Customs port, noting that its trading history dated back approximately a century. He also highlighted that Nigeria’s first indigenous and longest-serving Comptroller-General of Customs hailed from Calabar, underscoring the state’s historic contribution to the Service and the country’s commercial development. Adeniyi expressed optimism that the proposed port, alongside the modernisation of strategic border corridors, would create opportunities for investment, expand exports, generate employment and stimulate economic activities across the region. However, he stressed that infrastructure development must be accompanied by operational reforms, noting that the construction of ports and border facilities alone would not eliminate existing trade bottlenecks. He disclosed that the Nigeria Customs Service had conducted a Time Release Study to determine how long it takes to process consignments at the ports and identify areas requiring improvement in cargo clearance. The Customs CG also identified the establishment of effective One-Stop Border Posts at the Mfum-Ekok and Seme borders as critical to improving cross-border trade, eliminating duplicate examinations and reducing cargo clearance delays. According to him, effective implementation of the initiative could increase trade volumes by as much as 70 per cent. He explained that modernising the border corridors would require supporting infrastructure, including warehouses, storage facilities, weighbridges and scanners, to improve cargo handling, operational efficiency and border management. Adeniyi said the Service had studied successful models of modern border operations in other countries, expressing confidence that proven practices could be adapted to Nigeria’s operating environment. He also emphasised the need to maximise the deployment of non-intrusive inspection technology, particularly scanners, to facilitate legitimate trade, minimise unnecessary physical examinations and strengthen enforcement against smuggling and other illicit activities. item.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. item.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
item.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. item.title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated. The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election. Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State. “When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked. ﻿ Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election. “Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said. Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls. Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric. Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command. “Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said. Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state. However, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership.
